## Result

**Fused single-kernel CUDA implementation** for `alpha * a + b`.

| Metric (median of 7 samples x 100 iters) | Time | Ratio vs compiled |
|---|---|---|
| torch.compile baseline | 66.08 µs | 1.00x |
| eager baseline | 52.81 µs | — |
| **candidate (cuda_extension)** | **18.06 µs** | **0.273x (≈3.7x faster)** |

Requirement was ≤ 0.95x; achieved 0.273x. Verification: `[PASS] 1..5` (atol/rtol 1e-2).

## Implementation

`kernels/axpy.cu` (pure CUDA, no PyTorch deps):
- `axpy_vec4_kernel`: one `float4` (16 B) load of each input per thread, `fmaf(alpha, a, b)`, one `float4` store → 128 floats = 32 lanes = **exactly one warp, one block**, 1 vector load pair + 1 vector store.
- `__ldg` on both inputs (read-only cache), `__restrict__` pointers, FMA instead of mul+add.
- Runtime-tunable block size via `config` (0 = 32 threads/warp default, 1 = 128, 2 = 256) so tuning needs no recompile.
- Fallback scalar kernel for unaligned pointers or `numel % 4 != 0`, with alignment check on all three pointers.
- Launched on `c10::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream()`.

`kernels/axpy_binding.cpp`: validates CUDA/float32/contiguous/equal-numel with `TORCH_CHECK`, allocates with `torch::empty_like` (documented path only, no ATen internals), forwards to the C launcher. Registered via `REGISTER_BINDING`.

`model_new.py`: constructor signature preserved (`alpha: float`, no params → `state_dict` empty, `load_state_dict` from `Model` works); `forward` does exactly one custom-op call, with the bound function cached at module level.

## Optimization analysis / what was measured

This workload is 128 floats — entirely **launch/CPU-overhead bound**, not bandwidth bound. I verified this empirically with instrumented variants (compiled once, selected via the `config` argument with no recompilation):
- **No-launch variant** (empty_like only, kernel skipped): ~10.2 µs/call floor → per-call Python/pybind/allocation overhead dominates; the actual kernel adds only ~4 µs.
- **Cached-output-buffer variant** (avoid `empty_like`): ratio 0.27 vs 0.256 — statistically indistinguishable, so I kept the semantically safe `torch::empty_like` allocation instead of aliasing an internal buffer.
- Because GPU work is irreducible (one minimum-duration kernel launch), further kernel-level tuning (tiling, more warps, CUDA graphs) cannot help here; the remaining time is Python `nn.Module.__call__` + pybind + launch latency on this WDDM platform.

`kernels/` contains only the final implementation (`axpy.cu`, `axpy_binding.cpp`); all debug/no-launch/buffer-cache experiments were removed, and compile, verification and benchmark were re-run on the exact final files.
